habitat: Looping animation formats: GIFs, video intros, loading screens.
diet: Feeds on repetition — an eight-bit loop built to be watched far longer than any single viewing requires.
predators: None litigated to a loss. The joint suit with Keyboard Cat against Warner Bros. and 5th Cell settled on terms favorable enough that Warner Bros. later became a licensee rather than an adversary.
transmission: Embedded and looped rather than reposted as a still; virality here is duration, not distribution.
cause_of_death: None. Domesticated rather than killed — see status: corporate.
resurrection: Not applicable; it never stopped looping.
host_population: Anyone needing an ambient, high-energy visual loop, expanded after 2013 to the rights holder's own licensees.
mutation: Officially licensed variants now compete with the original for attention — an unusual case of the rights holder out-mutating the fans.
prognosis: The most commercially settled specimen in Volume II, and a realistic anchor-licence candidate per Integration Spec section 9.
enforcement_history: Joint suit with Keyboard Cat against Warner Bros. and 5th Cell filed April 2013 over Scribblenauts. Settled October 2013 on undisclosed terms, with Warner Bros. subsequently taking a licence.
curatorial_note: Owner is reachable, has licensed before, and has an established price. A realistic candidate if you ever pursue an anchor licence.
